_doc: RDL ladder state. Occurrence counts by family, and the rung each family has reached. Written by scripts/rdl.py, read by CI.

git_lock_family.last_signature: sovereign-infra/.git/index.lock dated 2026-08-20 13:59, and qesis-mcp/.git/index.lock created 17:36 by this session's own diagnostic git call. git add -A returned 'Unable to create index.lock: File exists'; the failure was redirected into a log; the next line asked whether anything was staged, correctly received no, and reported a clean tree.

cleared.reason: Enumerates the full L-115 lock set plus per-branch ref locks, refuses where it cannot unlink, and runs before staging in the lander. The occurrence that opened rung 4 cannot recur silently.

guard_not_executed.last_signature: audit_ecosystem.py rendered its 'What is failing' bullets with an em dash. The report is committed to ops/AUDIT_REPORT.md in both repositories by the lander, and sovereign-infra's compliance.yml runs qesis_agents/style.py over every .md on every push. The doctrine gate existed and the writer never ran it on its own output, so the 01:08Z landing, green on every required check, carried a red 'verify' onto main. The writer was subject to a gate it did not execute.

success_literal_not_measured.last_signature: audit_ecosystem.py marked main check conclusions PASS on sovereign-infra while the value it had just fetched read heal: failure and qesis-integrity: failure, and marked open pull requests PASS while listing PR 71 as CONFLICTING DIRTY; it forced the row's exit to 0 by hand. The row's verdict came from the exit status of gh, an operation, and never from a predicate over the value the operation returned. The report was built to be the thing the operator opens instead of trusting a sentence, and its own verdict column was a sentence.

cleared.reason: Fourth occurrence opened D-116 (a verdict is a predicate over a parsed value, never the exit status of the fetch) and landed it: audit_ecosystem.py has exactly two row constructors, gate() and measure(); every measurement carries its predicate on the row, unparseable is FAIL, no predicate is INFO, required checks come from the branch ruleset.

duplicate_id_from_stale_accessor.last_signature: next_lesson_id() read verify_ledger_singleton.py, which reads the ledger. The three entries were being written to a pending file, not to the ledger, so the maximum never advanced and all three commands allocated the same id. An id is allocated the moment it is written anywhere a later process will read it, and the allocator was counting only the committed store.

superseded_artifact_left_runnable.last_signature: LAND_EVERYTHING.bat revision 2 and LAND_EVERYTHING_FINAL.bat revision 3 were both executable in the same directory. The operator double-clicked the first. Revision 2 carried the tangled-branch strategy revision 3 existed to replace, so sovereign-infra PR 35 was reopened on the same unmergeable branch and the DAG defect repeated. The fix had been written and was not the file that ran.

gate_blocks_on_history_not_delta.last_signature: qesis-integrity is a required status check on main. The gate failed on historical constants rather than on the delta introduced by the change under review, so it would have failed every run forever and made every future pull request unmergeable. The only available remedy would have been switching the gate off, which is L-063 reached by construction rather than by neglect. Verified before landing: the gate returned exit 1 against a ledger whose defects were all already recorded.

obeyed_without_counsel.last_signature: The operator instructed removal because the GitHub API had rejected --auto. The rejection was caused by enablePullRequestAutoMerge being toggled off in the repository settings, not by the flag being wrong, and on a branch with a required status check --auto is the only strategy that can succeed because it queues the merge behind the check. Removing it converted a settings problem into a permanent merge failure, and PR 72 is the measured consequence. The operator is not a specialist in this and said so; supplying that reasoning was the job.

claim_from_proxy_not_resource.last_signature: audit_ecosystem.py section C asserted the ruleset's required contexts and treated every other check as informational; gh_ops.py proof filtered check names for the words integrity, heal and binding. compliance.yml's job is named verify, so the doctrine gate, the credential scan and the concordance check were invisible to both readers. The 01:08Z run ended with VERDICT GREEN and PROOF clean while Continuous compliance verification #138 had failed on main. The proxy was a list of words; the resource is the set of jobs in .github/workflows.

paired_what_is_not_pairable.last_signature: selfheal.yml step 'Install runtime' runs 'python -m pip install -r requirements.txt' unguarded. qesis-mcp has requirements.txt; sovereign-infra has none. In sovereign-infra the heal job failed in eight seconds, every hour and on every push, before a single control ran, and the run list read as a red loop rather than as a missing file. The workflow was carried across as one file because SH-7 wants one runner serving both repositories, and nothing asked whether every path the file names exists on both sides. The same move as L-170 (a checkout name mirrored as a contract) and L-171 (a script imported that exists in one repository only).

cleared.reason: C-5 refuses an unguarded requirements install whose file is absent from this repository; the gate runs in both integrity workflows and proves its three fixtures before judging (L-175)

stale_artifact_left_live.last_signature: The amputation step named PR 34 and 35 literally and covered only sovereign-infra. qesis-mcp PRs 71, 72, 73 and 75 accumulated, each with auto-merge armed and conflicts, each producing check runs and notifications for work nobody intended to land. The operator was shown a red PR 71 four rounds after it was superseded, while being told the task was finished. A cleanup keyed to numbers someone typed is not a cleanup.

reasoned_from_memory_not_docs.last_signature: The agent reasoned about auto-merge, required status checks and rebase provenance from memory. The official documentation states plainly that all merge conflicts must be resolved before a pull request can merge and that the merge button is deactivated until they are, which means arming auto-merge on a conflicted branch produces a pull request that can never fire. GitHub also publishes mergeStateStatus, an enum that answers exactly the question the agent kept guessing at: CLEAN, UNSTABLE, BLOCKED, BEHIND, DIRTY, DRAFT, UNKNOWN. Reading it once would have removed every merge failure of 2026-08-24.

gate_cannot_be_satisfied.last_signature: ECOSYSTEM_STATE.json carries repository, which build_ecosystem_state.py sets to ROOT.name. The file is generated once and mirrored into both repositories, and the checkout name differs between them by construction, so --check passed in qesis-mcp and failed in sovereign-infra on identical bytes. sovereign-infra's required status check qesis-integrity went red on main and stayed red, and its preflight failed with it. The L-166 repair one hour earlier had moved the measured blocks out of the comparison and left this one in.

cleared.reason: Third occurrence landed its gate in the same change set: build_ecosystem_state.py --selftest accepts drift in every volatile field including the checkout name and refuses a moved canonical path, a dropped hard constraint, and an absent or unreadable file; it runs as a step in qesis-integrity.yml of both repositories and inside test_gate.py.

shell_built_the_query.last_signature: LAND_EVERYTHING_FINAL.ps1 revision 5 read the pull request number with 'gh pr list --json number | ConvertFrom-Json | Select-Object -ExpandProperty number'. On PowerShell 5.1 ConvertFrom-Json emits the array as ONE Object[] item, Select-Object saw no 'number' property, the variable stayed empty, and every step keyed on it was skipped: merge_pr.py, ci_feedback.py, the MERGED read-back. Both pushes had succeeded. The summary line was built from the empty variable and said NOTHING DONE for both repositories. Second occurrence of the shell interpreting structured data: L-167 was PowerShell expanding a jq expression before gh saw it.

cleared.reason: LC-1 to LC-5 refuse a lander that parses JSON, hands gh a query, carries non-ASCII, hardcodes its landing or restores the whole tree; seven fixtures; the lander runs it on itself first (L-176)

bot_identity_blocked_the_deploy.last_signature: selfheal.yml set user.email to selfheal@qesis.invalid. RFC 2606 reserves .invalid precisely so it never resolves, and Vercel refuses to deploy a commit whose author it cannot identify: 'The commit author email (selfheal@qesis.invalid) is not a valid email address. This prevents Vercel from identifying the commit author and allowing the deployment.' The operator was shown that dialog and told to fix his own git config, which was never the failing identity.

disk_snapshot_taken_as_repository.last_signature: Revision 5 captured the working tree as a holding commit, cut the branch from origin/main and ran 'git checkout <snapshot> -- .', restoring every tracked file from the operator's disk. The disk is the source of the session's changes, not of the repository: the self-heal loop and the daily ops report commit to main from a runner (SH-7, G-07), and the setting that lets them is now on (L-174). The next click would have reverted each of those commits with a green summary. Found by reading the lander before its next run, not from a loss; nothing had ever landed from a runner, so nothing had been reverted yet.
